## 19. Next step — V1.40

The next brick should descend from cache identity into **cache lifecycle and
cross-surface invalidation**, without inventing a new color transform.

### V1.40 micro-scope

1. audit every production `ResolutionCache` instantiation and lifetime;
2. verify whether caches are component-local, scene-local or process-global in real
   callers;
3. audit cache reuse across graph rebuilds;
4. prove stale `RuntimeGraph` detection before cache lookup;
5. measure LRU eviction under realistic component counts;
6. test cache pressure with 1 / 10 / 100 / 1,000 distinct resolution identities;
7. audit whether geometry-cache and resolution-cache dependencies can drift apart;
8. compare resolution fingerprint and geometry dependency fingerprint ownership;
9. audit cache behavior when a relation is added/removed rather than merely mutated;
10. audit cache behavior when parent hierarchy changes;
11. verify cache isolation between sibling-targeted effects;
12. test concurrent read/write behavior without introducing single-flight prematurely;
13. decide whether cache statistics need an explicit reset/snapshot API;
14. inspect whether serialized resolution fingerprints need a formal schema/version
    envelope before any persistence feature is added;
15. generate a larger before/after cache visual board covering hierarchy, relation,
    consequence and direct-context mutations;
16. keep the COLOR boundary unchanged unless a distinct real production color
    consumer appears.

No new HSL/OKLab/XYZ operation, gamut mapping, lighting, grading or renderer color
pipeline belongs to V1.40 unless independently discovered and contractually frozen.
